Foods & ingredients with edible gold

Edible gold is a culinary decoration sold as thin leaf or flakes for foods such as chocolates and cakes. Use only products explicitly labeled edible and intended for food; craft leaf and wrappers are different.

    Contains real edible gold

    Eight Swiss chocolate truffles decorated with real edible gold turn a chocolate gift into a tiny treasure presentation. The gold is a culinary finish on the chocolate.

    Material / ingredients: Chocolate truffles decorated with pure edible gold, according to the maker. The gift box is not edible.

ORIGINAL GOLD TRAILS IDEAS

Make your own little gold rush

These are kitchen ideas, separate from the products above. Use food ingredients and kitchen bowls, spoons, and tools only. Keep real soil, paydirt, gold pans, and other prospecting equipment away from food preparation.

Gold-rush cupcakes

Make a little claim on top of a familiar cupcake, using a crumb landscape and candy treasure.

Gather: Baked cupcakes · Frosting · Crushed food-grade cookies · Gold-colored nugget candy or unwrapped chocolate coins

  1. Spread frosting on cooled cupcakes.
  2. Scatter cookie crumbs to suggest a gravel bar.
  3. Add the candy treasure after removing any wrappers.

Original Gold Trails idea; not a product listing or a tested recipe. Use clean kitchen utensils and edible ingredients; keep real soil and prospecting equipment away from food.

Treasure-chest dessert cups

Turn a small dessert into a treasure chest with biscuit sides and a few edible coins.

Gather: Prepared pudding or another ready-to-eat dessert · Food-safe serving cups · Biscuits or cookies · Unwrapped chocolate coins

  1. Spoon the prepared dessert into clean serving cups.
  2. Use biscuits as the sides of a small chest.
  3. Tuck unwrapped chocolate coins into the top just before serving.

Original Gold Trails idea; not a product listing or a tested recipe. Use ordinary serving dishes, not real panning or digging tools.

Edible cookie-crumb paydirt

Hide candy nuggets in cookie crumbs for a dessert-table gold hunt. The only dirt in this claim is pretend.

Gather: Crushed cookies · Gold-colored candy nuggets · Clean food-safe bowls · Kitchen spoons

  1. Crush cookies in a clean food-preparation bowl.
  2. Fold in the candy nuggets.
  3. Portion into food-safe bowls and uncover the candy with kitchen spoons.

Original Gold Trails idea; not a product listing or a tested recipe. Never add real soil, sand, paydirt or material from prospecting equipment.

A few notes before following the trail

Gold Trails links out to the maker, seller, or operator. This collection is research, rather than hands-on product reviews. Listings, prices, menus, and stock can change; a source page does not guarantee checkout, shipping, or a place on today’s menu.

Gold-colored food, real edible gold, and removable foil packaging are labeled separately. Check the product’s ingredient, allergen, and food-use information before choosing it.
